label: GPT-6 Astra
output:
Tolu, me o 😂 Biology 100L here, and Medicine and Surgery was what I applied for too. I wrote JAMB in 2025, scored 251 and got offered Biology at a federal uni here in Lagos. So when you asked for somebody who is actually inside it, I said let me answer because this was literally me last year.

First, sorry about how you’re feeling. I’m not going to tell you “at least you got admission” as if that will suddenly stop the disappointment. The day I saw Biology on my portal, I locked myself in my cousin’s room in Surulere and cried. I didn’t eat. You know when you’ve already pictured yourself doing one thing and then the portal just gives you another plan? That was me. My mum even continued telling people in church that I was studying Medicine for like two months 😭 I had to beg her to stop because ah, mummy, that is not what they gave me.

So I understand why you’re crying. It doesn’t mean you think Biology students are useless or that you’re ungrateful for admission. You wanted something badly and got something else. It’s painful.

But let me give you the transfer gist properly, because both “transfer is a myth” and “just read hard” are leaving out important things.

**Transfer to Medicine is real, but it is NOT automatic.** What our level adviser told us is that, to transfer to MBBS after 100L, you need a CGPA of at least **4.5 out of 5, and there must be space**. That second part is very important. It’s not “once I get 4.5, they must take me.” You can work hard and meet that CGPA requirement, but space is still another matter.

She told us that last year, about six people got moved into Medicine from the whole faculty. Not six from Biology alone o, the whole faculty. She thinks over 40 people applied. I’m telling you what she told us, not claiming I personally checked everybody’s records, but that should give you an idea of why nobody should sell it to you like a sure route.

Our adviser also said you need to meet the Medicine cut-offs in **JAMB and post-UTME**. So your 268 alone doesn’t establish whether you’re eligible for transfer. I don’t know your school’s cut-offs or what you scored in post-UTME, and I don’t want to use my own school’s information to mislead you. You need to check both.

That’s why I don’t agree with Kingsley saying transfer is a myth. Not knowing anybody who transferred in his set doesn’t mean it never happens. But favour’s “just read hard” is also too simple. Reading hard matters, yes, but there are requirements and available spaces that motivation alone cannot settle.

Let me even use myself as an example. My first-semester CGPA is **4.31**. Not 4.5. I’m still trying. I came in knowing the target, and I still haven’t reached it yet. So I cannot come here and tell you “accept, get 4.5, transfer” like I’m describing three easy steps. I’m inside the thing, and I know the work it takes.

For 100L, we’re doing BIO 101, CHM 101, PHY 101, MTH 101 and GST. Please don’t hear Biology and think you’ve escaped Physics and Maths 😂 Those two are the ones dealing with people. You still have to take the other courses seriously, not only the Biology courses you like. If you’re aiming for that kind of CGPA, you can’t just decide that Maths is not your business.

There are practical expenses too. My lab coat was ₦6,500, dissecting kit was ₦9,000, and the practical manual was extra. Those are what I paid, not a price list for your school, but I’m mentioning them so you have a small picture of the actual course beyond admission and transfer talk.

Now, is Biology bad? Honestly, no. I’m enjoying it more than I expected, especially genetics and cell biology. That surprised me because I entered with my mind still very much on Medicine.

Our first BIO practical, we dissected toads. One guy in my group fainted, and somehow I was fine. That was the day I caught myself actually being interested in what we were doing. I remember thinking, wait, I actually like this thing. Before then, I’d been so focused on the course I didn’t get that I hadn’t really given the one in front of me a chance.

That doesn’t mean one practical made me forget Medicine or that you must fall in love with Biology because I’m beginning to enjoy it. It just means Biology itself wasn’t the terrible thing I’d built up in my head while I was disappointed. It’s a proper course, not just a place to sit while waiting for MBBS.

For me, the important question before accepting is: **if the transfer doesn’t happen, would you be willing to continue studying Biology?** You don’t have to be excited about it immediately. I wasn’t. But if your entire reason for accepting is “I will definitely leave after 100L,” please pause and get the facts first. Nobody can honestly promise you that transfer.

About rewriting, I won’t tell you it’s wrong either. If Medicine is genuinely what you want and you’re ready to prepare again, that’s a valid option. But people say “just stay home one year” as if that year is always easy and the next admission is guaranteed.

My secondary school classmate, Ifeoma, rejected Pharmacy to rewrite for Medicine. She has written JAMB two more times and she’s still at home. I’m not telling you that to scare you or say her decision was stupid. Her own experience doesn’t mean yours will go the same way. It’s just why I can’t casually tell somebody “rewrite, one year is nothing.” Sometimes it ends up being more than one attempt, and you need to think about whether you’re ready for that uncertainty too.

Before your acceptance deadline, please go to your faculty or department and ask for the **exact transfer rules for your own school**. Ask whether Biology students can transfer into MBBS after 100L, the CGPA requirement, the JAMB and post-UTME requirements, how available spaces affect selection, and when and how applications are made. If there’s an official written policy, ask where you can see it.

Don’t just trust forum people, including me. I can tell you my experience and what our adviser said, but I’m not your school’s admissions office. Your dad and aunty may both mean well, but you need something more solid than either “you’ll transfer” or “you can never transfer.”

And one question to ask yourself quietly, without everybody answering for you: do you actually want to study and practise Medicine, or do you mainly want to be “doctor” for your parents? It can be a mixture, so I’m not judging you. My own mum was announcing Medicine in church when I was already in Biology, so I know how family expectations can enter somebody’s head. Just try to separate what you want from what everybody will be happy to announce.

My honest answer is that I can’t choose accept or rewrite for you. Accepting Biology can make sense if you’re willing to study it even if transfer doesn’t work out. Rewriting can make sense if Medicine is what you really want and you’re prepared for another attempt without a guarantee. Neither choice makes you a failure.

Cry if you need to, but use the time before the deadline to get proper information too. You don’t have to pretend you’re happy with Biology today. I wasn’t happy either, and now there are parts of it I genuinely enjoy. Whatever you decide, this admission result is not the end of the world, Tolu. It hurts now, but you still have options.
